chapter_title: Chương 280: Ông chủ thực sự có tầm nhìn.

segments.title: Chương 280: Ông chủ thực sự có tầm nhìn.
segments.content:
Chen Guiliang was very busy in October, occupied with establishing the VIE structure.

This structure basically involved using a company registered in the Cayman Islands as the entity for the US IPO. Then, through a series of shell companies, a VIE agreement would be used to control the actual company within China.

This was to circumvent China's policy restrictions, without which a public listing would be impossible.

The state maintained a tacitly permissive attitude towards this, neither encouraging nor obstructing it.

Chen Guiliang's main job was to discuss the details of the structure with venture capital firms and company executives, and sign the WFOE establishment documents and VIE agreements, among other things.

The equity distribution had to be confirmed again, including the stock options for executives and long-time employees.

There were also the aggressive clauses Chen Guiliang had signed with the VCs during the Series A and B financing rounds to maintain control of the company. If any of them violated US regulations, they had to be completely nullified.

The entire process would take a month.

And that was only because ByteDance's equity structure was simple and clear. For companies with complex equity compositions, it could take two to three months of wrangling.

The next step was to formally register in the Cayman Islands.

Chen Guiliang's part was signing the documents in China; the rest was left to the head of the IPO and the law firm.

Around December, they could begin the financial compliance rectification. This usually took three to six months.

Given ByteDance's situation, it would probably take at least four months. This was mainly due to its involvement with Bailian Technology and Tudou.com.

Bailian Technology owned the cash cow "Reign of Might," which had a positive impact on ByteDance's listing and could even be considered one of the core cornerstones of its IPO valuation.

But Tudou.com was a double-edged sword.

Tudou.com had plenty of room for growth and a high valuation from VCs, something they could boast about during the roadshow. But in reality, it was a money pit, kept alive by burning cash, which would have a negative impact during the SEC review.

Moreover, Tudou.com, Xiaonei.com, and Hainei.com had once cross-promoted each other to drive traffic. This could be considered related-party transactions, which would also take time to audit in detail.

There were many other details, including making back payments for employees' social security.

Fortunately, Chen Guiliang had long been providing social security for his employees, so this back-payment step could be skipped entirely. In contrast, most domestic companies at the time had to go through a whole ordeal of making back payments before their IPO.

Once all this was done, around early summer next year, Chen Guiliang would have to start IPO financing negotiations.

"Hey, Brother Gang, I need to tell you something," Chen Guiliang called Tao Chenggang.

Tao Chenggang was busy on his end. "Go ahead."

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm preparing for the IPO, and we'll be doing financial compliance rectification next year. A team will be coming to your company for an audit, so you'll need to get ready."

"Sure thing, you're going public!" Tao Chenggang was pleasantly surprised. "Don't you worry, I recently hired a highly-paid financial director. My ragtag operation is becoming more formal. Just give me a call a month or two in advance, and I'll have the finance department prepare early."

Chen Guiliang said, "OK, thanks."

"What's the relationship between us? Don't be such a stranger," Tao Chenggang said.

Chen Guiliang asked, "How's 'Reign of Might' been doing lately?"

Tao Chenggang said, "The peak concurrent user count has been rising, but the growth has slowed down noticeably recently. Damn it, 'Zhengtu' and 'Eudemons Online' are constantly fighting for market share. But their growth doesn't seem to be that fast either. After all, the existing market is only so big. Like Shi Yuzhu, I'm now expanding into smaller cities and counties."

In last month's online game rankings on 17173.com, the top two spots were still held by the unshakable "World of Warcraft" and "Fantasy Westward Journey."

Third was "Zhengtu," and fourth was "Reign of Might."

"Legends of the Three Kingdoms," having passed its period of explosive public attention, had dropped from third to fifth place.

Following them were "Westward Journey Online II," "Audition," "The World of Legend," and "Crazyracing Kartrider."

Tencent's "QQ Fantasy" continued its decline and was about to fall out of the top ten.

The improving performance of "Reign of Might" and its month-over-month revenue growth would make it easier for ByteDance to raise funds and go public.

Even if ByteDance hadn't received cash dividends yet, the profits corresponding to its shareholding could be directly consolidated into ByteDance's financial statements or recorded as investment income, thereby increasing ByteDance's overall net profit and earnings per share.

In comparison, Tudou.com was a bit of a letdown.

Chen Guiliang called Wang Wei again to ask about Tudou's current situation.

What situation could there be?

Registered users were growing, view counts were increasing, and they were quietly accumulating copyrights.

With the money raised from financing early this year, Tudou.com could hold on for another four or five months. Wang Wei planned to start the next round of financing in a while.

Tudou.com's greatest enemy had, in fact, already emerged.

Youku was currently in its trial operation phase and was expected to officially launch by the end of the year at the latest. Moreover, its founder had an impressive background, and many VCs were scrambling to throw money at Youku.

Oh, right, and there was also Zhubajie.com.

ByteDance's angel investment had secured a 25% stake in Zhubajie.com!

Chen Guiliang had almost forgotten about this. After he made contact with Zhu Mingyao, he had delegated the rest of the negotiations to his staff.

Chen Guiliang immediately called Zhu Mingyao to ask about the situation.

Zhu Mingyao laughed heartily. "Mr. Chen, I thought you had stopped caring about Zhubajie.com."

"How's the website been doing lately?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Zhu Mingyao said, "Including me, the entire company only has six people. Working from dawn till dusk, our net profit last month was estimated to be a few thousand yuan. I'm currently working on landing a big 300,000 yuan contract, a project for an education group."

"I've more or less settled things with the person in charge, but the leader who needs to sign off on it doesn't quite trust Zhubajie.com. He said the website's name itself sounds unprofessional. Fortunately, I used to be the chief reporter for the Evening News, so that identity still carries some weight. I had a drink with that leader, and he said as long as a reputable media outlet reports on Zhubajie.com, he'll sign the contract."

"What does he mean by reputable? This time I contacted CCTV, and not just any program, but 'Xinwen Lianbo'! The CCTV reporter has already come and filmed. They're willing to promote us because this is a new internet model proposed by a Chinese person. Once 'Xinwen Lianbo' airs, we'll definitely get that 300,000 yuan contract, and our website will become famous nationwide."

Chen Guiliang said with genuine admiration, "Mr. Zhu, you're amazing."

Zhubajie.com had been profitable since its launch. After the report on "Xinwen Lianbo," its revenue would grow rapidly.

This would also have a positive effect on ByteDance's IPO.

The IPO was a priority, but the company also needed managing.

Chen Guiliang called in Xie Yang and others from product and publicity to discuss how to adjust and improve the Groups feature on Xiaonei.com.

Cai Yifei, the second programmer the company had hired externally, had transitioned from being a pure programmer to a key member of the product department who also handled technical matters.

This guy's thinking was particularly agile. Since joining, his technical skills hadn't improved much, but he had become increasingly adept at expanding and refining product content.

Chen Guiliang said, "The Groups feature on Xiaonei.com was just an add-on at first. Now, more and more content is being generated. What are your thoughts?"

Xie Yang said, "The situation with Xiaonei Groups is a bit awkward. It's somewhere between Douban and Baidu Tieba, but leans more towards Douban. I don't think it needs to be changed, nor can it be changed. As for improving it, we just need to enhance our on-site search capabilities."

Cai Yifei said:

"Once our on-site search engine becomes more powerful, we can still make some changes. Right now, Xiaonei Groups are mainly formed among classmates, schoolmates, and friends. The social ecosystem of Xiaonei is already closed, and this makes the groups even more so."

"We need to break the closure between schoolmates and friends and get student users from across the entire site to interact. For now, we can start by expanding from 'same school' to 'same city,' one step at a time. We shouldn't try to imitate Douban or Tieba. Xiaonei Groups are Xiaonei Groups; we're different from both of them."

Several others also shared their opinions.

Chen Guiliang thought it over carefully and felt that Cai Yifei's point was very valid.

Forcing it to lean towards Douban or Baidu Tieba would likely cause backlash from Xiaonei users.

After some more discussion, Chen Guiliang accepted Cai Yifei's proposal.

Then, Chen Guiliang said, "Since we're making that change to Xiaonei Groups, I plan to launch another new product. This product won't belong to Xiaonei or Hainei, but will be a separate website."

"Users of Xiaonei and Hainei won't need to register again. They can log in directly to the new site with their existing accounts, though they'll be able to change their nicknames on the new site."

"On the new website, users can ask questions, and other users will provide answers. It will use a point system. Points can be obtained by topping up or earned by answering questions."

An employee named Qi Tao said, "Isn't that just Baidu Zhidao?"

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "Baidu Zhidao is Baidu's derivative, a practical Q&A tool. Both questions and answers are quick and simple. What I want to create is an elite community knowledge platform, focusing on in-depth knowledge sharing and discussion, with answers that are more like structured, long-form articles and professional analysis."

"Where are we going to find so many elites to answer questions?" asked an employee named Weng Fanyu.

Xie Yang laughed. "Peking University, of course. When I don't understand something, I often pretend to be a student and go ask those Peking University professors."

Chen Guiliang said, "University professors are one source, but there are also other successful people in society. Those successful individuals also have a desire to express themselves, especially in their areas of expertise. When the time comes, I'll personally invite them."

Cai Yifei asked, "What should the new website be called?"

Someone said loudly, "It could be called Lantai Wen. Old stories of Lantai, new questions from today's people. Lantai was the Han Dynasty's book repository, and the Tang Dynasty's Secretariat was also called Lantai. Modern related institutions also use Lantai as an elegant name."

As soon as he said this, everyone objected.

"Bro, that's too high-flown. It's not that being literary is bad, but your name isn't easy to remember."

"You guys from the Chinese department should really stop showing off your erudition."

"What Lantai Wen? Jixia Academy would be a better name."

Chen Guiliang raised his hand and said, "Alright, let's not argue anymore. I've already thought of a name for the website. Let's call it Zhihu."

It was just as literary, but the boss was definitely right.

"Zhihu? That's a great name. Firstly, it's easy to remember, a homophone for 'zhī hū zhě yě'; secondly, it's meaningful, 'zhī hū' means 'do you know?' It perfectly fits the website's positioning."

"The boss is a genius at naming things. Whether it's ByteDance, Game Science, or the upcoming Zhihu, they all embody a romantic sentiment of literature and science."

"Don't you guys forget, when the boss got into Peking University, he was specially admitted for the New Concept Composition Competition."

A bunch of brown-nosers.

But Chen Guiliang found it quite pleasant.
